Formulation
[Primary concern is extensive eczema worsening over a few days with significant itchiness and dryness. Previous treatments included creams and low-potency steroid (Hydrocortisone), with inadequate control prompting the introduction of stronger topical steroids and antihistamines. The patient has a history of asthma and family history of hypothyroidism and migraines, which may influence management choices.]

Mental Health Care Plan Details
Principal Problem: Eczema
- Patient Goal(s): Alleviation of severe itching and reduction in skin rash
- Clinical Goal(s): Stabilize and improve skin condition, prevent eczema exacerbation
- Actions (Patient): Apply prescribed Betnovate and Fexofenadine as directed; continue current emollients
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe Fexofenadine and Betnovate; follow up in two weeks or sooner if no improvement

Secondary Problem (if applicable): Asthma
- Patient Goal(s): Maintain control over asthma symptoms
- Clinical Goal(s): Prevent asthma exacerbations related to skin allergies or treatments
- Actions (Patient): Use blue inhaler as needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Monitor any impact of skin treatment on asthma control

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Application of topical treatments, monitoring for adverse reactions
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased itchiness, spread of rash, or allergic reaction
- Coping Strategies: Maintain regular emollient use, avoid potential allergens, contact GP if issues arise
